ingredientSections.heading: Pistachio Pesto
items: 1 Cup Pistachio nuts, shelled and dry roasted

methodSections.heading: Salmon Wellington
steps: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Cut the salmon fillet into 4 equal portions.

Take a sheet of filo pastry for each piece for salmon and brush lightly with melted butter. In the centre of each sheet place two basil leaves and then place a piece of salmon on the basil. Sprinkle a pinch of salt and pepper on the salmon.
Coat the salmon with a couple of teaspoons of Dijon mustard. Finely chop the cranberries and smash the almonds in a pestle and mortar and then sprinkle both over the salmon.

Fold the filo pastry over the salmon, making wrapped parcels. Brush all sides of the parcels with butter, covering completely and cook in a fry-pan on a medium heat until both sides are golden and crispy. Finish the cooking by baking in the oven for roughly 10 minutes.

methodSections.heading: Pistachio Pesto
steps: Blend all ingredients except the cream in a blender or food processor until smooth adjusting the quantity of oil if necessary. Optionally, make a larger batch, store in the fridge for up to 2 weeks and use with other dishes.
When the salmon is ready to serve, stir together and warm the pesto and cream in a saucepan.

methodSections.heading: Serving
steps: Pour the warmed creamy pesto on a plate, cut the salmon parcels in half and place in the pesto. Serve with steamed or roasted vegetables.
